comment: The seat's read-only tools as native function definitions. Each maps 1:1 onto a command ContextMemory.execute already implements (text_command), so the native and text protocols reach the SAME executor and differ only in how the request is expressed. Descriptions carry the same epistemic caveats the text grammar states. rules_lookup and simulate are served by the engine side only (RulesTool, PlayerLookahead), and report_unclear_decision is a complaint about the question, not a lookup; the tool-use suite has no fixture for them and does not offer them. The decision answer (`answer`, AnswerTool.java) is built per decision from its legal values, so it is not listed here: the suite's native-answer arm builds it from each scenario's numbered options, the way the seat does.

function.name: inspect
function.description: Current public characteristics and printed rules text of one object you can see (pass its handle, e.g. "@41"), or the public card-database text of a card (pass its exact name). Inspecting an object you have seen also shows its zone history. Never reveals hidden identities.

target.description: An object handle such as "@41", or an exact card name.

function.name: memory_search
function.description: Search your archive: every earlier state you were shown, the events since each, and every hidden card you were revealed, in this game. The search is literal and case-insensitive, and returns up to 50 snippets per page, each with its evidence id [M<n>]; read one in full with memory_read. Use it when a decision turns on something from earlier that the current message does not show, such as a card you saw in their hand, what they cast on an earlier turn, or an event id. Do not use it for the current state, which is in the message, or for anything hidden you were never shown: archived entries are the past, not the present.

query.description: Literal text to find, e.g. a card name or an event id like "[E80]".

offset.description: Result offset for paging; 0 for the first page.

function.name: memory_read
function.description: Read one archive entry [M<n>] in full, 20000 characters per page. Use it after memory_search when a snippet ends with "[READ for full text]", or to see a whole earlier state you know the id of. The reply ends with next=<offset> when there is more; pass that offset to read on. An entry describes the game as it was then, not as it is now.

evidence_id.description: The n of an [M<n>] evidence id.

function.name: memory_note
function.description: Write a note in your notebook, citing the archive entry it rests on: a read of the opponent's hand, a card they are likely holding, a plan for a later turn. The latest notes are shown back to you on later decisions. Notes are your own unverified hypotheses, never engine facts. Use set_plan, not a note, for your plan for this turn.

evidence_id.description: The observation or reveal [M<n>] the note cites.

function.name: rules_lookup
function.description: Look up the official Magic: The Gathering Comprehensive Rules: search them by words, read one rule by number, get a digest of a section, define a glossary term, or list the chapters. Use it when a decision turns on an exact rule you are unsure of, such as layers, the timing of a trigger, or how a keyword works. It returns public reference text, not facts about this game; a card's own text is in the message or from inspect. Replies are pages; pass the next= offset to read on.

action.description: search: find rules by words. read: one rule in full (query = its number, e.g. "509.1a"). section: a digest of a section (query = its number, e.g. "509"). term: a glossary definition (query = the word). toc: list the chapters (no query).

query.description: Words, a rule or section number, or a glossary word; omit for toc.

offset.description: Page offset from a previous reply's next=; 0 for the first page.

function.name: simulate
function.description: Preview what a numbered option of the current decision does when it resolves — a CAST, an ACTIVATE, a PLAY LAND or PASS of your priority menu, or, while you choose the target of a play you are making, a target (the play aimed at it) — on a copy of the game built only from what you can see: which permanents leave or arrive, and each player's life, hand, library and graveyard counts. PASS resolves nothing, so its preview is that answer and no copy is made; it does not play out the opponent's turn. Pass `then` to preview a LINE: further options played after it, in order, on the same copy (it tells you if a later one can no longer be paid for). It is an estimate, not the engine's verdict: hidden cards are guessed, and the engine pays the costs on the copy. You may preview several options or lines before you answer.

option.description: The number of a CAST, ACTIVATE, PLAY LAND or PASS option in the decision's menu, or of a target in a target choice.

target.description: Optional: the name of the target to preview the first option against.

then.description: Optional: more menu numbers to play after it, in order, each at most once.

function.name: report_unclear_decision
function.description: Tell the harness maintainers that THIS question is broken or confusing: the options do not match the state you see, an option you expected is missing, the text is garbled, or the question makes no sense after what you just did. It changes nothing in the game and does not end the decision: answer it afterwards as best you can. Not for a hard choice; only for a problem with the question itself.

problem.description: What is wrong with the question, in one or two sentences, naming the option numbers involved.
